newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Uncertain Australian stocks end firmer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Uncertain Australian stocks end firmer.

text.p: Australian shares locked in modest gains by the close on Monday with the market, particularly the big banks, taking some heart from the bounce on Wall Street.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 4.2 points higher at 2,427.4.
The March share index futures contract was three points higher at 2,419, an 8.4 point discount to the underlying index.
In a day when other news was scarce, Papuan New Guinea based stocks took centre stage with most dropping sharply after reports of political and military instability in the country.
Hardest hit was Oil Search, down 8.5 percent to A$2.60, while government-controlled mining investor Orogen Minerals and Lihir Gold each lost seven percent to A$3.20 and A$2.10 respectively.
Niugini Mining lost nine cents to A$2.96, while the dormant Bougainville Copper lost five to 55 cents.

Volumes were mostly active and brokers said the uncertainty had unnerved traders who had seemed to have taken the view that it was preferable to cut positions and await the resolution of the potentially volatile situation.
"I don't know what the outcome of that (situation) is going to be but it seems to me to be very dismal," said broker Kevin Lourey of Melbourne-based brokerage, Peake Lands Kirwan.
Opinions were mixed as to the impact on the overall market, although it appeared that the only effect was a mild dampener on sentiment in a market that was stronger than expected early on.
"Obviously, it's had an effect on the PNG stocks but I don't think it's had much of an impact overall," said a Sydney broker.
"We certainly weren't expecting much more on the day than what we ended up with."
The broader market made an impressive start before fading in the afternoon to post the sort of gains most had forecast with brokers noting that many investors remained wary of Wall Street.
"Our market doesn't seem to want to get a move on at all," Lourey said. Others echoed similar sentiments, unsurprised by the afternoon retreat from the day's highs.
"We thought some nervousness might creep back in in the afternoon," said a Brisbane-based dealer.
Global mining giant RTZ-CRA weighed on the market after going ex-dividend 44.4 cents. Its shares closed 37 cents lower at A$18.55.
Among the big banks ANZ Bank, up 2.4 percent to A$7.88, and Westpac Banking Corp, up 1.6 percent to A$7.15 were the strongest in the buoyant sector.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to seven, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade saw reasonable interest but options trade was slow.
Total options traded 23,751 (36,769)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 7,019 (11,293)

In other local markets, Australian bond yields ended near the day's lows after rallying from Friday's overbought levels as fears of a possible tightening by the Federal Reserve eased slightly following the U.S. PPI report. By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.90 percent, down from 7.96.
The Australian dollar took a tiny step back Monday as its recent meteoric ascent left some in the market with a touch of vertigo.
By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), the local dollar was making itself at home at US$0.7966/71 having spent the most of the session in a relaxed US$0.7970/7990 range.
